questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

Abu said that __he saw the picture__.

options.text: he will have seen the picture
he would have seen the picture

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **he had seen the picture**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is divided into two clauses.
 
• The conjunction (**that**) joins the parts of the sentence.
 
• Whenever two clauses are joined by a conjunction and one is written in the **simple past tense**, the other one must be written in the **past perfect tense**.
 
• The **past perfect** refers to a time earlier than before now. It is used to make it clear that one event happened before another in the past.
 
• The structure follows: **Subject + had + v3+ object.__**
 
• So, "**had seen**" should be used in the given sentence.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

 

**Corrected sentence:** *Abu said that he had seen the picture.*

questions.question:
**Complete the following collocation.**

I was running late so I only had time for a _______ shower.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **quick.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Collocation is the combination of words formed when two or more words are often used together in a way that sounds correct.
 
• Let us look at the meaning of the given words.
 
 
• **Quick**: Moving fast or doing something in a short time. (Used to indicate '**time**')
 
• **Hasty**: Done something in a hurry, sometimes without the necessary care or thought. (Used to indicate '**urgency**')
 
• **Fast**: Moving or capable of moving at high speed. (Used to indicate '**speed**')
 
• **Short**: Measuring a small distance from end to end. (Used to indicate '**length**')
 
 
 
• In this sentence "**running late**" is already mentioned with reference to time.
 
• So, as per the usage and meaning of the given words "**quick**" should be used here.
 
• **A quick shower** means washing oneself in a short period.
 
• The implied meaning of the sentence is: I was running late, so I could only take a brief shower.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

**Complete sentence:** *I was running late so I only had time for a **quick**__ shower.*

questions.question:
**Select the correct active form of the given sentence.**

Her phone can’t be switched off by my father.

options.text: My father switches off her phone.
My father could not switch off her phone.
My father have not switched off her phone.
My father can’t switch off her phone.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **My father can’t switch off her phone.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The given sentence is in the passive form and we need to change it into the active **form**.
 
• ​Both the sentence use a modal verb** 'can'.** The structures for active/passive voices for modal verbs are:
 
 
• ​Passive: Object + Modal verb + be + Verb (IIIrd form) + by + Subject
 
• Active: Subject + Modal verb + Verb (Ist form) + Object
 
 
 
• Example - 
 
 
• Active voice - *We can buy diamonds, but we cannot buy sympathy.*
 
• Passive voice - *Diamonds can be bought but sympathy cannot be bought.*
 
 
 
• Rules of Conversion from Passive to Active Voice:
 
 
• Identify the subject, the verb, and the object.
 
• Change the object into the subject.
 
• Change the verb into the past participle form of the verb.
 
• Change the subject into an object.
 
 
 
• ​Therefore, the correct answer is option 4.

 

Correct Active Voice: *My father can’t switch off her phone.*

questions.question:
**Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.**

Shyam asked me how I had persuaded his sister.

options.text: "How are you persuading my sister?” Shyam asked me.
"How did you persuaded my sister?” Shyam asked me.
"How did you persuade my sister?” Shyam asked me.
"How have you persuade my sister?” Shyam asks me.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **"How did you persuade my sister?” Shyam asked me.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The given sentence is an **in****direct **speech and we need to convert it to a direct speech.
 
• When we change an indirect speech to a direct speech, we must follow these rules:
 
 
• The reporting verb remains unchanged in the case of a question.
 
• The inverted commas ("...") are placed to show the indirect speech part.
 
• The comma (,) is added after the sentence covered in inverted commas in direct speech.
 
• The first word of the direct speech should be in capital letters.
 
• The past perfect "**had + v3**" changes to "**did + v1**" in the direct speech to form the **simple past tense**.
 
• The pronoun '**I**' and '**his**' changed to '**you**' and '**my**' respectively in the direct speech.
 
 
 
• Thus, option 3 is the correct answer.

 

Hence, the direct speech is - *"How did you persuade my sister?” Shyam asked me.*

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

One can never imagine / how hot it gets in Delhi / unless one doesn’t go / there in person.

options.text: how hot it gets in Delhi

questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: **unless one doesn’t go**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error here lies in the **third part **of the sentence.
 
• Replace "**doesn't go**" with "**goes**" to correct the sentence.
 
• The conjunction '**Unless**' means** ****except on the condition that or under any other circumstance than.**
 
• So, we cannot use a negative word after '**unless**' as it conveys a negative meaning itself.
 
• Also, **'goes' **will be used as the subject is singular.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2** which contains an error in it.

 

**Corrected sentence**: *One can never imagine how hot it gets in Delhi unless one goes there in person.*

• Statement S is the third sentence of the passage which explains that the island was built by King Zainul-Abi-Din.
 
• Statement Q is the last sentence of the passage which shows that Wular Lake is also considered to be a relic of Satisar Lake from ancient times.

The correct answer is option 4.

questions.question: **Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: able

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let's look at the **meaning **of the given words.

 
 
• Brave: Ready to face and endure danger or pain; showing courage.
 
• Consistent: Acting or done in the same way over time, especially so as to be fair or accurate.
 
• Able: Having the power, skill, means, or opportunity to do something.
 
• Oblige: Make someone legally or morally bound to do something.
 
 
 
• So, as per the usage of the given words "able" is the most appropriate option.
 
• The implied meaning of the sentence is: We must be capable of controlling our emotions while driving.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is option 3.

 

Complete passage: *All drivers are affected by road rage, whether they are directly or indirectly (1) involved.__ Individual coping qualities **__(2) __**__influence__ the behaviour of stressful drivers. Instead of being enraged over circumstances beyond their control, drivers __(3) must__ learn to be patient. On the road, we must be **__(4) able__** to control our own emotions. Road raged drivers are also more likely to (5) __________ more traffic offences.*

questions.question: **Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: incur

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let's look at the **meaning **of the given words.

 
 
• Drag: Pull someone or something along forcefully, roughly, or with difficulty.
 
• Reflect: To show, express, or be a sign of something.
 
• Incur: Become subject to something unwelcome or unpleasant as a result of one's own behaviour or actions.
 
• Proceed: To begin a course of action.
 
 
 
• So, as per the usage of the given words "incur" is the most appropriate option.
 
• The implied meaning of the sentence is: Road raged drivers are also more prone to committing traffic violations.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is option 3.

 

Complete passage: *All drivers are affected by road rage, whether they are directly or indirectly (1) involved.__ Individual coping qualities **__(2) __**__influence__ the behaviour of stressful drivers. Instead of being enraged over circumstances beyond their control, drivers __(3) must__ learn to be patient. On the road, we must be __(4) able__ to control our own emotions. Road raged drivers are also more likely to **__(5) incur__** more traffic offences.*
